::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 29th 1878  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54921: 74
:::

Miss Yonge would be obliged if [Messrs Macmillan](organizations/other_111.qmd) would send to 

the [Revd R Bigg Wither](people/person_2318.qmd)
St Thomas’ Home
Basingstoke

a copy of each of 

[The Heir of Redclyffe](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd)
[Heartsease](cmy_books/cmybook_19.qmd)
[The Daisy Chain](cmy_books/cmybook_24.qmd)
[The Trial](cmy_books/cmybook_53.qmd)
[Pillars of the House](cmy_books/cmybook_109.qmd)
[Scripture Readings with comment](cmy_books/cmybook_87.qmd)
[Pupils of St John](cmy_books/cmybook_72.qmd)

---

**Note:** The Rev. Reginald Bigg Wither was a nephew of the Rev. William Bigg Wither, curate of Otterbourne, and he published in 1887 a *History of the foundation and of the chief incidents in the gradual establishment of St. Thomas' Home, Basingstoke, the Winchester Diocesan Penitentiary for Friendless and Fallen Women*.  CMY evidently selected works she thought would interest the inmates.
